I learn by building. DocSage asks a simple question: when code changes, can the documentation notice? Feastrek asks something more practical: how should a group of trekkers eat when budget, weight and altitude all pull in different directions?

Everything here is early, and I’d rather show that honestly than dress it up.

DocSage

Keep documentation in sync with code.

A local-AI-powered documentation synchronization tool. It compares versions of Python repositories or GitHub pull requests, identifies public API changes, and flags outdated Markdown sentences.

OllamaGemma · gemma4:e2b defaultPython reposGitHub PRsMarkdown
WHAT IT DOES

It reads two versions of a Python project, finds changes to the public API, then checks your Markdown for sentences that no longer match. The model runs locally through Ollama, so no cloud service is involved.

v1 — api.py

def load(path, strict=False):def parse_cfg(path):def render(doc):

v2 — api.py

def load(path, strict=True, cache=None):# parse_cfg removeddef render_doc(doc):

README.md

By default load() skips errors (strict=False). Pass a path to read a file. Use parse_cfg() to read your settings. Call render(doc) to build the page.

Feastrek

Smarter meal planning for trekking groups.

An intelligent meal-planning tool for trekking groups. It optimizes three meals per day around budget, pack weight, altitude-related fuel requirements, ingredient freshness, and medical conditions.

BudgetPack weightAltitude fuelFreshnessMedical conditions
WHAT IT BALANCES

Three meals a day, planned together: cost, what the group has to carry, the fuel needed to cook at height, which fresh ingredients to use first, and the medical needs of people in the group.
